boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the Nitro SDK's mb_fileinfo.c, 0x0206736c..0x02067ee4: 10 functions, gapless in config/arm9/delinks.txt. Each is identified by its body against ntrtwl/NitroSDK libraries/mb/src/mb_fileinfo.c, and seven of the ten compile byte-identical from the SDK's own text (IsAbleToLoad, MBi_IsAbleToRecv, MBi_get_blockinfo, MBi_MakeBlockInfoTable, MBi_SetSegmentInfo, MBi_ReadSegmentHeader, MBi_MakeDownloadFileInfo); MB_GetSegmentLength, MB_ReadSegment and MB_RegisterFile are the same functions before the SDK added the segment cache.

Order: mwccarm emits the bodies in reverse. The SDK's file order of the surviving functions is MB_GetSegmentLength, MB_ReadSegment, MBi_ReadSegmentHeader, MB_RegisterFile, MBi_MakeDownloadFileInfo, MBi_SetSegmentInfo, MBi_MakeBlockInfoTable, MBi_get_blockinfo, MBi_IsAbleToRecv, IsAbleToLoad, and the ROM holds exactly that reversed. MB_UnregisterFile and MBi_get_blocknum, which sit between them in the SDK, are absent: nothing calls them.

notes: HAND-BUILT manifest entry, not tools/tubuild.py create output: tu_map does not segment arm9.

Built as C, like the SDK and the other mb TUs (MB_GameInfo.c). The SDK's constants and MbSegmentType are mb_fileinfo.c's and mb_child.h's own and stay in the source; the shared types (MB_CommPWork, MbParentFile, MB_BlockInfoTable, MBDownloadFileInfo, MBGameRegistry, RomHeaderView) are in include/private.

This SDK is older than the ntrtwl/NitroSDK copy: no segment cache (MBiCacheList), so MB_GetSegmentLength is the header, authentication code and two static modules with no minimum, MB_ReadSegment reads both modules whole and the authentication code after them, MB_RegisterFile passes that code's address to MBi_MakeDownloadFileInfo as a third argument, and MB_ReadSegment does not patch _start_AutoloadDoneCallback.
MB_ReadSegment's own-binary path writes the 16 MiB default into the ROM header at HW_ROM_HEADER_BUF itself (the later SDK keeps it in a local).

MB_RegisterFile's sequence counter is the SDK's function-local `static u8 update` at 0x020a9d28 (one byte, then three bytes of alignment before mb_gameinfo.c's mbss at 0x020a9d2c). The source names it data_020a9d28 as an extern: dsd sizes a .bss symbol to the next symbol (0x4), while tubuild requires the object's .bss contribution (0x1) to fill the claim, so the one-byte static cannot be owned until tubuild accepts trailing .bss alignment.
